origin.description: Time-series and scatter plots for a zoo series, including lines.zoo and points.zoo.
origin.usage:
plot.zoo(x, y = NULL, screens, plot.type, panel = lines, xlab = "Index", ylab = NULL, main = NULL, xlim = NULL, ylim = NULL, xy.labels = FALSE, xy.lines = NULL, yax.flip = FALSE, oma = c(6, 0, 5, 0), mar = c(0, 5.1, 0, if (yax.flip) 5.1 else 2.1), col = 1, lty = 1, lwd = 1, pch = 1, type = "l", log = "", nc, widths = 1, heights = 1, ...)
lines.zoo(x, y = NULL, type = "l", ...)
points.zoo(x, y = NULL, type = "p", ...)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A zoo series. lines.zoo and points.zoo use the same object.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: NULL draws the series against its index. A second univariate series is an inner-join scatter of y against x. lines.zoo with y draws the outer join, first column against second.

arguments.name: screens
arguments.text: Which panel each series uses. A missing screens follows plot.type. A supplied screens is expanded with make.par.list and turned into a factor.

arguments.name: plot.type
arguments.text: "multiple" or "single". When it is missing and screens is missing, the code chooses "multiple". When screens is supplied, length(unique(screens) == 1) is the number of levels, so any non-empty screens chooses "single". More than one level still opens several panels. plot.type "multiple" with one screen resets to one panel per series.

arguments.name: panel
arguments.text: Function called as panel(index, column, col, pch, lty, lwd, type). The default is graphics::lines. A custom panel can read panel.number, series.number, series.within.screen, nser, and nr from the parent frame on a multiple plot.

arguments.name: ylim
arguments.text: On a multiple plot, a list is one element per panel, in panel order. A pair is kept, including a reversed pair. Any other length is replaced by its range. NULL on a drawn panel is not a finite window. On a single plot, a pair is kept and a longer vector is ranged.

arguments.name: xy.labels, xy.lines
arguments.text: Scatter labels. A logical xy.labels sets both the labels and the default of xy.lines. A character vector is drawn as text. The code then sets xy.lines from that logical flag, so character labels still draw lines unless xy.lines is FALSE.

arguments.name: col, lty, lwd, pch, type
arguments.text: col, pch, and type go through make.par.list, so a length-1 style stays length 1. lty and lwd are recycled with rep to the number of series.

arguments.name: nc, log
arguments.text: nc defaults to 1 for up to four panels and 2 otherwise. log is "x", "y", or "xy" on the drawn axes.

origin.details: A missing type is "l" for a time series and "p" for a scatter with no labels. The recorded coordinates are the values passed to the panel or to the scatter, not the expanded plot window. points.zoo is lines.zoo with type "p". The default panel uses points when every type is "p" and lines otherwise.
origin.value: The merged series, invisibly. The check records the panel or scatter coordinates.

translation.description: Time-series and scatter plots for a Zoo series, including lines_zoo and points_zoo.
translation.usage:
plot_zoo(x, y=None, screens=None, plot_type=None, panel=None, xlab=None, ylab=None, main=None, xlim=None, ylim=None, xy_labels=False, xy_lines=None, yax_flip=False, col=1, lty=1, lwd=1, pch=1, type=None, log="", nc=None, widths=1, heights=1, draw=True)
lines_zoo(x, y=None, type="l", ...)
points_zoo(x, y=None, type="p", ...)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A Zoo series. Column names, when set, are the series names used by named styles.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: None draws the series against its index. A second univariate Zoo is an inner-join scatter. lines_zoo with y draws the outer join, first column against second.

arguments.name: screens
arguments.text: None means the argument was missing. A supplied value is expanded with make_par_list and turned into a factor.

arguments.name: plot_type
arguments.text: None means missing. The same screens rule as plot.zoo applies: a non-empty screens selects "single", and more than one level still opens several panels.

arguments.name: panel
arguments.text: None uses points_zoo when the type is "p" and lines_zoo otherwise. A custom panel receives the index and the column. On a multiple plot, plot_zoo sets panel_env before the call.

arguments.name: ylim
arguments.text: Same list, pair, and range rules as plot.zoo. The coordinate record stores the pair or null, not the 4 percent margin.

arguments.name: xy_labels, xy_lines
arguments.text: Same scatter rules as plot.zoo. Character labels still draw lines unless xy_lines is False.

arguments.name: col, lty, lwd, pch, type
arguments.text: A dict or a list of (name, value) pairs is a named R list. An empty name is an unnamed element. def_ in make_par_list is R's def.

arguments.name: draw
arguments.text: True draws with Matplotlib. False returns only the coordinates and is the timed call.

translation.details: Matplotlib draws the figure. The comparison is the coordinate text. A length-1 style is not expanded to one value per row. log changes the axis scale of the figure and not the recorded numbers.
translation.value: A dict of panel or scatter coordinates. With draw=True it also holds the Matplotlib figure.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from zoo.series import Zoo
from zoo.plot import plot_zoo
chart = Zoo(np.array([[1, 2, 0], [3, 2, 1], [2, 4, np.nan], [5, 3, 2], [4, 6, 3]], dtype=float), [1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
chart.colnames = ["A", "B", "C"]
plot_zoo(chart, type="b", pch=[("A", [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]), ("B", 3)], col=[("C", 4), ("", 2)], draw=True)
